text: GENEVA "SCENE."

label: text
text: ASSAILANT ARRESTED.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Count Bethlen, the Hungarian Premier, was the victim of an assault by a Hungarian who burst into the room where the Lengua holds session, and sharply slapped Count Bethlen's face, shouting "That's on behalf of the Hungarian nation."

label: text
text: Geneva, June 10.

label: text
text: The Italian delegate rescued Count Bethlen from his assailant, who was arrested.

label: text
text: Bethlen's assailant, who is named Dejusth, is the Secretary of the Hungarian Republican Party, and obtained a ticket of admission as a journalist. He declared when arrested he "wanted to build a criminal."

label: text
text: A later message from Geneva says that Count Bethlen was attacked while attending a private committer dealing with the question of ending the financial control of Hungary. The assailant was a Hungarian Republican.

label: text
text: Count Bethtlen's hotel yesterday was guarded by detectives at his request.

label: text
text: It is noteworthy that while the League Council yesterday agreed that the financial control of Austria should terminate at the end of June, it is still considering the question of ending the financial

label: vision_footnote
text: Mr. Jeremiah Smith

label: text
text: control of Hungary, although Sir Austen Chamberlain, on Tuesday, stated that Mr. Jeremiah Smith, the League's Commissioner-General, considered his task ended.

label: text
text: There has been an extraordinary anti-Hungarian outburst in the French Press arising out of the proceedings at Geneva, particularly on account of the letter M. Briand sent to the League Secretariat recommending that the international convention suppress the currency of forgeries. Although M. Briand did not mention Hungary, his letter is described by French newspapers at a rebuff to Court Bethlen, "and his band of Pretorians and country gentlemen ruling by, terror."

label: text
text: Some French newspapers attack Britain for her "partial" attitude towards Hungary.

label: text
text: Hungary's Finances.

label: text
text: The League Council adopted the report of the Committee on the financial reconstruction of Hungary recommending the cessation of the functions of Mr. Jeremiah Smith from July 1.

label: text
text: M. Dubois, Chairman of the Committee, pointed out that Mr. Smith's departure from Hungary did not mean the end of League control in respect of the balance of the Reconstruction Loan, amounting to 83,000,000 gold crowns, and the revenues assigned to the service of the loan, but the abolition of control of the Budget.

label: text
text: Count Bethlen expressed the gratitude of the Hungarian people for the effort resulting in successful financial reconstruction in the short space of two years and a half.

label: paragraph_title
text: Spain and Article Four.

label: text
text: At the League Council the Spanish representative announced that Spain would ratify the amendment to Article IV of the Covenant of the League relating to the re-election and rotation of non-permanent members of the Council.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain congratulated the Spanish Government, and said that the announcement would be received with great satisfaction and appreciation.

label: text
text: Spain's action completes the required ratifications and the amendment will thus become operative.

label: text
text: The Brazilian delegate, Senhor Mello Franco, has lodged Brazil's resignation from the League Council. This does not imply that Brazil will cease membership of the Lengua.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL CRISIS.

label: text
text: WHY RUSSIAN GOVERNMENT SENT MONEY.

label: text
text: FOREIGN OFFICE SATISFIED.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: London, June 10:

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, in reply to questions, Sir W. Joyson-Hicks, Secretary of State for Home Affairs, said that the Foreign Office was satisfied that the Russian Government had sent money to Great Britain for the purposes of the general strike (Ministerial cheers).

label: text
text: Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, Labour Leader, pointed out that the strike leaders had refused that money.

label: text
text: Sir W. Joyson-Hicks continued that money was sent to the Miners' Federation by some very closely co-related bodies in Russia comprising the Soviet Government, the Third International, and other organisations, though he had not yet established that the Soviet Government itself had directly sent the money.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAILWAY SMASH.

label: text
text: TERRIFYING SPECTACLE AT CLAREMONT.

label: text
text: SPLENDID RESCUE WORK

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Capetown, June 10.

label: text
text: The train involved in the railway disaster was the express from Capetown to Claremont conveying citizens to their suburban homes at the close of the day's work.

label: text
text: When the coupling of the train broke on the bridge at the entrance to Salt River the rear part became derailed and jolted its way into the station, presenting a terrifying spectacle.

label: text
text: Two coaches were caught on the pillars of the bridge and the compartments were smashed to splinters.

label: text
text: Many workmen on the platform immediately rendered first aid, amid scenes of terror, pending the arrival of expert help. Splendid rescue work was done, and the injured passengers were rapidly hurried to three hospitals. All except one are doing well.

label: paragraph_title
text: LORD STEVENSON.

label: text
text: DEATH OF KILMARNOCK. MAN

label: text
text: The death is announced of Lord Stevenson.

label: text
text: [Lord James Stevenson, who was 53 years old, was Chairman of the Standing Committee of the British Empire Exhibition. He was Managing Director of John Walker and Sons (the well-known whisky distillers), Kilmarnock During the War he was a member of numerous Ministerial Committees in an honorary capacity. He has no heir.]

label: paragraph_title
text: FRENCH FINANCE.

label: text
text: MINISTER OPTIMISTIC.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Paris, June 10.

label: text
text: Heard by the Finance Committee of the Senate, M. Peret stated he had decided to avoid inflation and hoped to balance the Budget for 1927 without new taxes. The Government have drafted a plan, in defence of the franc, and the gold reserve at the Banque de France remains, and will remain intact.

label: text
text: The Minister recommended the restoration of confidence by political appeasement, and fiscal prudence would remove in time restrictions against the export of capital.

text: IN JEOPARDY

label: text
text: A COMPROMISE BILL

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin, June 10:

label: text
text: In the Reichstag, submitting a compromise Bill on the question of the property of the ex-rulers, Chancellor Marx, declared that the demand for confiscation without compensation was against the principles of a legal State and against the Constitution conferring on all citizens equal rights.

label: text
text: He added that if a plebiscite resulted in the negative the Govern-

label: text
text:

Below: WITHHEIM MARK

label: text
text: ment would do its utmost to reach a settlement in the spirit of the compromise Bill. It would not hesitate to take the consequences if it was impossible for Reichstag to reach an agreement.

label: text
text: A Centre Deputy, on behalf of the Government Parties, approved of the Bill.

label: text
text: The Socialist, Herr Muellen, attacked President Von Hindenburg regarding his recent letter opposing expropriation without compensation and saying that President Hindenburg was guilty of unconstitutional partisanship.

label: text
text: Chancellor Marx would not admit that President Hindenburg had violated his constitutional position. But this attitude is not shared by all the Government Parties, including the Centarists, which Chancellor Marx is chairman.

label: text
text: The compromise 'Bill was finally referred to the Judicial Committee.

label: text
text: " QUEEN'S ROAD STIR.

label: text
text: Some excitement was caused in Queen's Road near the Queen's Theatre yesterday afternoon during the early performance of the picture by police whistles which drew the usual crowd.

label: text
text: A Chinese was arrested by an Indian constable after a chase down the road.

label: text
text: It was reported that the man had snatched some money from a person at the Theatre and bolted What actually happened was that the man went there and insisted on a free seat. What transpired later was the result of the man having to be pushed out.

label: paragraph_title
text: TOOLS, NOT CARGO.

label: text
text: The licensee of a native passenger craft pleaded "not guilty" at the Marine Court this morning, to a charge of using the boat for carrying other than passengers' effects. The defence was that the "cargo"—a quantity of planks and ropes—were "tools" used by painters who had worked on board the s.s. "Mausang" and the workmen were returning to shore with their implements.

label: text
text: Another boat-owner was fined $5 for a similar offence, which was admitted.

text: HOME MAILS

label: text
text: About 1,000 bags of mails were dealt with by the Post Office yesterday morning.

label: text
text: The arrivals were 63 bags by the s.s. "Arafura" from Australia and Manila; 325 bags including transhipment mail by the s.s. "Karmala" from Europe also 82 bags of London parcels; 468 bags from the U.S.A. and ports by the s.s. "President Cleveland" included in which were a number of bags from Europe via Siberia. Malis also arrived from Shanghai and Singapore by other vessels.

label: paragraph_title
text: HAWAIIAN JUDGE.

label: text
text: (Router's American Service.)

label: text
text: The death has occurred of Judge Sanford Ballard Dole.

label: text
text:
Sanford Ballard Dole.
[Judge Dole was born in the Hawaiian Islands," on April 23, 1844; his parents being American missionaries. He was educated at Oahu College, Hawaii, and Williams College, Massachusetts. He studied law in Boston, and was admitted to the Bar there. He engaged in practice in Honolulu, and was a member of the Legislature in 1884 and 1886; and was a leader in the reform movement of 1887. He was appointed Judge Supreme Court, 1887-9; placed at the head of the provisional government in 1893; becoming President of the Republic of Hawaii in 1894 holding office till 1900. When President Cleveland, in December, 1893, through Minister Willis, demanded that he should relinquish to Queen Lillie Kalani her constitutional authority, he replied, denying Cleveland's right to interfere. He was a strong advocate of the annexation of Hawaii to America, and in January, 1898, visited America in that behalf. He was Governor of Hawaiian Territory from 1900-1903; District Judge, District of Hawaiian Territory from 1903-15; and appointed by President McKinley-a-member of commission to recommend to Congress legislation concerning the Hawaiian Islands.

label: paragraph_title
text: KOREAN FUNERAL

label: text
text: DISTURBANCE CAUSED BY STUDENTS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Tokyo, June 10.

label: text
text: A message from Seoul says the Korean funeral procession was thrown into confusion this morning when nearing the burial place by about forty students who attempted to distribute inflammatory literature amidst much shouting.

label: text
text: The students were arrested, but the Korean crowds lining the route took up the shouts, thereby adding to the disturbance.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW SHANGHAI COUNTRY HOSPITAL

label: text
text: The grounds and buildings of the new Country Hospital, 17 Great Western Road, said to be the finest hospital of the Far East, with the possible exception of the Rockefeller Foundation in Peking, will be open for inspection of the public on Saturday Sunday and Monday, June 12, 13, and 14, from 10 a.m. to noon and 3 p.m. to 5 p.m.

label: text
text: The hospital will care for 125 patients but the exact date for the admission of the first patient has not yet been determined. Funds to erect the hospital were made to the Shanghai Municipal Council by an anonymous donor and the hospital is estimated to be worth about Tls. 1,500,000.

label: text
text: In addition, the donor has given the interest on £40,000 for certain wards and will give Tls. 10,000 for running expenses the day the hospital opens.

label: paragraph_title
text: DR. KOO'S ATTITUDE.

label: text
text:
HIS INDIFFERENCE TO CHANG
WU CONFERENCE

label: text
text: Peking, May 27.—In order to show his non-partisan attitude, Dr. Wellington Koo denies that he will leave Peking for Poating to welcome Marshal Wu Pei-fu. Regarding the coming Chang Tao-lin conference, it is interesting to note that Marshal Wu advised the "government" of his departure from Hankow for the North on the morning of May 26, adding that he will discuss all state questions with Dr. Yen personally in a few days; but on the other hand, Marshal Chang has entirely ignored the Yen, agency-cabinet by leaving the Premier in the cold as to his movements. Up to the present, not one telegram has been received from Mukden about Chang Tso-lin's departure for Tientsin although both private and semi-official messages indicate that the Manchurian warlord is leaving Mukden on the 29th instant for Tientsin where he will meet his new sworn brother from Hankow without visiting Peking.

label: paragraph_title
text: AMERICAN PAPER CURRENCY MADE SMALLER.

label: text
text: Washington, June 2.—The size of American paper currency will soon be reduced to the same dimensions as the peso bills now in use in the Philippines, according to a high-official—of the Treasury-Department. It is learned that Secretary Mellon is seriously considering a proposal of this nature.

label: text
text: William A. Dupuy, a government currency expert told the United Press that the new bills would be similar to these now in use, with the dimensions of all lettering and figures reduced by about one-third. He said that smaller currency would save the government $3,000,000 annually in manufacturing costs.

label: text
text: He said that the designs now under consideration were the result of an order by Elihu Root when he was Secretary of State under President McKinley, approving a type of currency for the Philippines, similar to American bills but smaller.

label: text
text: Herbert D. Brown, chief of the bureau of efficiency and chairman of the committee studying paper money, understands that Secretary Mellon is strongly in favour of the- plan.
